transcript.text: Hey there, superstar! Woohoo, fractions are so much fun! How is your awesome day going? Have you been playing any cool sports or hanging out with friends today? You've got this math problem totally covered! To get from 3 to 6 on the bottom, what do we multiply by? Whatever you do to the downstairs number, you have to do to the upstairs number too! What do you think? Go get 'em, champ!

Oh, you absolute rockstar! High five! You nailed that first one completely, 4/6 is spot on! Woohoo! You are on such an amazing roll today! 

Now, look at you tackling 2/9 plus 4/9 like a true math champion! Since both of those downstairs numbers are already best buddies and match, we just add the upstairs numbers together! What do you get when you add two and four? You are doing brilliantly, keep shining bright, superstar!
I no understand. Why bottom number stay same? This is too confusing.

Oh, my sweet math superstar, don't you worry for one second! You are doing so brilliantly! Imagine you have a pizza cut into 9 equal slices. If you have 2 slices and your best friend gives you 4 more slices, the slices don't magically change size, do they? They are still 9th-sized slices! We just count how many slices you have total! What do you get when you add 2 and 4? You've totally got this, champ!
Is it 6/18? I not understand pizza.

Aw, you are trying so hard and I am super proud of you! No worries at all about the pizza analogy, friend! Math can be tricky sometimes, but you are a brave champion! 

Remember, when the bottom numbers are the same, they just tell us the size of the pieces, so the bottom number stays a 9! 

If we keep the 9 on the bottom, what do we get when we add 2 and 4 on the top? You can do it!
is 6/9 because bottom stay nine and two plus four is six next: 1/4 + 1/8?

Yippee! You did it! 6/9 is an absolute touchdown, you genius! Woohoo! 

Look at you go tackling 1/4 plus 1/8 next! You are a total math machine today! 

Uh oh, look at those bottom numbers—they are sneaky and don't match! Just like our first puzzle, we need to make the bottom numbers the same best friends before we can add. Can you turn that 4 into an 8? What do we multiply it by? You've got this, superstar!
Is it 2/12? I not understand this.

Aw, you are trying your absolute best and I am so, so proud of you, champ! It is totally okay if this is tricky! 

Think back to our very first puzzle: to turn a 4 into an 8 on the bottom, we multiply by 2! Whatever we do downstairs, we have to do upstairs too. So if we multiply the 1 on top by 2, what do we get? 

You are an amazing superstar, and we are going to crack this together! Woohoo!
